name: Haskell
summary: Purely functional, non-strict (lazy) language with Hindley-Milner type inference extended by type classes; defined by the Haskell 2010 Report and, in practice, by GHC and its many language extensions.

level_notes.0: GHC is the de-facto implementation; its pipeline is Lexer.x/Parser.y -> renamer (GHC/Rename) -> type checker (GHC/Tc) -> desugarer (GHC/HsToCore) -> Core optimiser -> STG -> Cmm -> native/LLVM/JS/Wasm back ends, with the runtime system in rts/. The canonical repository is gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/ghc; links use the official github.com/ghc/ghc mirror. Hugs, MicroHs and UHC are independent implementations.
level_notes.1: The Haskell 2010 Language Report is the last committee standard (no ISO/ECMA standard). Modern Haskell is defined by the GHC User's Guide 'Language extensions' chapter and by accepted GHC proposals; System FC (docs/core-spec) is the formal core calculus.
level_notes.2: Real World Haskell (book.realworldhaskell.org) was unreachable from the research sandbox and is therefore not linked.
level_notes.3: The taxonomy has no 'monads' concept; monad material is tagged purity/input-output/statements (do-notation) where that is what the section covers.
